claims.text: Tesla Model S owner’s manual (Tesla.com) lists cargo volumes of front trunk 3.1 cu ft, rear cargo 25.0 cu ft with rear seats up and 61.4 cu ft with the rear seats folded (2025/2026 Model S specifications).

Independent reviews note the Tesla Model S uses adaptive air suspension and delivers a generally comfortable ride, but reviewers warn ride can feel firmer with the optional larger 21‑inch wheels. (The Car Connection review / specs pages discuss ride and wheel-size tradeoffs.)

Published specifications and data aggregators for the BMW 5 Series (G60) commonly list the sedan’s luggage/cargo capacity at about 520 liters (≈18.4 cu ft) with the rear seats up (expanding when the rear seats fold).

U.S. EPA / model‑specific listings used in databases show the 2025 BMW 530i (G60) 4‑door sedan luggage (trunk) volume listed as 14.0 cu ft for that specific U.S. trim — i.e., trunk volume can differ by model, powertrain and U.S. trim.

Comparing the two: the Tesla Model S provides substantially more practical cargo volume than the BMW 5‑series sedan in common U.S. specs (Tesla ~25.0 cu ft rear cargo vs BMW sedan U.S. EPA listings of ~14.0–18.4 cu ft depending on trim/powertrain).
claims.about: Comparison of Tesla Model S vs BMW 5 Series cargo volume

claims.text: Review coverage and press testing of the BMW G60 5 Series emphasize a quiet cabin, comfortable seats and a smooth ride (reviewers describe seat comfort and ride refinement among the car’s strong points).

Owner threads and technical parts pages in German BMW forums report the foot‑activated / ‘hands‑free’ Easy‑Open tailgate (berührungslose Heckklappe) can be omitted on some vehicles and — when present — owners commonly describe it as finicky or intermittently unreliable (forum examples and parts‑service notes document unreliability and diagnostic/repair items).

Technical parts/service documentation and aftermarket parts pages note failure modes for the sensor and control modules used by ‘easy‑open’ (foot‑activated) tailgate systems and explicitly list “Easy‑Open function works unreliably” as a reported symptom.
claims.about: Hands‑free tailgate sensor failure modes (BMW and similar systems)

claims.text: The Tesla Model S owner’s manual does not document a factory foot‑kick / hands‑free trunk-opening (kick‑sensor) feature — Tesla’s manual lists liftgate operation and adjustable opening height but contains no foot‑kick/‘hands‑free’ activation instructions, so the specific German complaint about an unreliable foot‑kick trunk does not describe a documented factory feature of the Model S owner’s manual.
claims.about: Applicability of 'hands‑free trunk' complaint to Tesla Model S
